query: What kinds of expenses tend to get declined, and does it differ by department?

per_column.name: asset_type_category
per_column.rationale: Categorising the asset/item type from short_description and ci is a reasonable grouping axis, though it describes WHAT was expensed rather than the decline reason directly. Values are mostly well-grounded readings of the text, though 'RAM component' mapped to 'peripheral' is a loose call.

per_column.name: asset_acquisition_context
per_column.rationale: The acquisition context (procurement vs auto_generated vs manual_registration) is only weakly relevant to why expenses get declined. More importantly, the source text rarely states this; labels like 'procurement' for an iPod service line appear to be invented distinctions not clearly warranted by the visible text.

per_column.name: travel_related_marker
per_column.rationale: A bare boolean flag; travel expenses are a plausible decline category, so it offers some analytical leverage, but as a single binary it is fairly generic. It is derivable from description text and largely grounded, though it duplicates the intent of the travel_equipment asset type.

per_column.name: device_brand
per_column.rationale: Brand extraction is a genuine new axis and mostly grounded where the text names a vendor (Dell). However confident brand assignments where the source is silent (e.g. 'AWS' for a generic 'Cloud Database Service' line) are unsupported inferences. Relevance to decline reasons is moderate.

per_column.name: department_requesting
per_column.rationale: This is trivially redundant with the existing original 'department' column, adding no new analytical leverage for a query already about departments. Worse, the produced values (e.g. 'Sales' for a RAM component line) are not derivable from the shown source text and appear fabricated or copied without grounding.

judge.rationale: The query is about WHY expenses get declined and how that varies by department. Asset-type categorisation gives some grouping value, and travel/brand flags add minor axes, but none directly capture decline reasons and several are only loosely tied to the analysis. department_requesting is essentially a redundant restatement of an existing column. Groundedness is mixed: brand and asset-type extractions are reasonable readings of the text, but acquisition_context and department_requesting assert specifics the visible source text does not support, indicating hallucination on several rows.
